Guidance & outlook: India continues to be the second largest producer of crude steel globally with 170.15 million tonnes (MT) in FY 2025-26 up 11.80% from 152.18 MT in FY 2024-25.

Further, India has retained its position as the world leader in Direct Reduced Iron (DRI) production, DRI production in India reached 60.49 MT in FY 2025-26, up 8.48% year-on-year from 55.76 MT in FY 2024-25, with the coal-based route accounting for nearly 85% of production.

Indiaʼs total finished steel production stood at 161.70 MT in FY 2025-26, registering a robust growth of 10.2% over 146.69 MT recorded in FY 2024-25, reflecting sustained expansion in the countryʼs steel manufacturing capacity and output.
Growth & demand: According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) - World Economic Outlook Update - July 2026, global economic growth is projected at 3.0% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, reflecting moderate but sustained expansion, supported by improving demand in emerging economies and gradual easing of inflationary pressures.

According to the World Steel Associationʼs Short- Range Outlook (SRO) - April 2026, global steel demand is projected to grow by 0.3% in 2026, followed by and accelerated growth of 2.2% in 2027 to reach 1,762 MT.
During FY2025-26, crude steel production grew around 11.18% and finished steel consumption grew 7.9% year-on-year, indicating continued strong underlying demand for iron ore and pellets.
Margins & costs: EBITDA for the year has increased by 138.72% to ₹4,098.02 Lakhs as compared to the EBITDA of ₹1,716.64 Lakhs achieved in previous Financial Year, reflecting the improved scale of operations and stronger operating performance.
Inflation Global headline inflation is expected to increase from 4.1 percent in 2025 to 4.7 percent in 2026 before declining to 3.9 percent in 2027.

Silico Manganese The Company has successfully commissioned its Silico Manganese Division, having an annual installed capacity of 29,403 MT and achieved a capacity utilisation of approximately 47% during the year.

The Company successfully commissioned a 30 MW power plant during the year, comprising 12 MW of Waste Heat Recovery Boiler (WHRB) capacity and 18 MW of Atmospheric Fluidized Bed Combustion (AFBC) capacity.
